title: Fourth reason: conformity to the law of nature belongs to pure nature, so the righteousness that makes it possible is natural
source_text: LV. Adde quod ad naturae dotes in creatura rationali non corrupta sed pura pertinet, ut conformis sit legi naturae, & ad illius regulas se componat. Ac proinde quicquid sine quo non potest naturae legi sese conformare, & omnes motus suos illi subdere, dotes & ordinem naturae non excedit. Ad legem autem naturae se componere non potest, homo destitutus omni justitia & sanctitate, & infirmitatibus illis quibuscum hodie nascimur, obnoxius. Adeoque sanctitas & justitia illa, per quam tolluntur tales infirmitates, ad naturae non corruptae dona spectare censenda est.
pass_a_gloss: Add that it pertains to the endowments of nature in a rational creature not corrupt but pure, that it be conformable to the law of nature, and compose itself to its rules. And therefore whatever without which it cannot conform itself to the law of nature, and subject all its motions to it, does not exceed the endowments and order of nature. But man destitute of all justice and sanctity, and subject to those infirmities with which we are born today, cannot compose himself to the law of nature. And so that sanctity and justice, through which such infirmities are removed, must be judged to regard the gifts of nature not corrupt.
pass_b_english: Add that it belongs to the endowments of nature in a rational creature that is not corrupt but pure to conform to the law of nature and shape itself by its rules. So whatever it needs in order to conform to the law of nature and bring all its impulses under it does not go beyond the endowments and order of nature.

But a man without any righteousness or holiness, and subject to the weaknesses we are born with today, cannot shape himself by the law of nature. So the holiness and righteousness that remove such weaknesses must be counted among the gifts of uncorrupted nature.

lemmas.gloss: the endowments and order of nature

choices.english: whatever it needs in order to
choices.why: The printed 'quicquid sine quo' is elliptical ('whatever [is that] without which'); the English gives the sense.
